speaker: Lieutenant Frank Drebin
clickReplies: Report first. Conversation second. Use MISSION REPORT on the office computer, print it, then bring it here.
wrongItemReplies: That is not a report. I admire your confidence, not your filing skills.
alreadySubmittedReplies: I have already filed that report. Once was quite enough.

lines: A mission report. Finally, a visitor with supporting documentation.
You included the attachments. All of them. That is either competence or a cry for help.
Filed. You may now ask questions. Brief ones. The cabinets are listening.
You filed every attachment. I almost respect you. Almost.
Help me sort these index cards. Match each document to its department.
Use SORT INDEX CARDS when you are ready. The cards can wait. They have no social life.
JM-041? Yes. John McClane's field report. An artifact recovery operation that went wrong.
One entry for the general archive. Another for restricted storage. Same report number, different access rules.
That does not tell us what happened to him. It tells us someone did not want the whole file on the same shelf.
Start with the ordinary records. And do not confuse 'restricted' with 'please help yourself'.
People think an archive is where information goes to die. Nonsense. It comes here to be mislabelled.
When you are ready for more fieldwork, use NEXT MISSION.
